data.name: TransPlan
data.detailed_description:
Entregue uma caixa do ponto A ao ponto B com apenas algumas ferramentas simples e as leis da física. Crie rampas e catapultas, veja os objetos rolarem e caírem, e de alguma forma ... de alguma forma chegar ao destino. Cada projeto é um quebra-cabeça desenhado à mão para com o qual você possa interagir - Elabore um plano, experimente e faça acontecer!

O Transplan apresenta dezenas de projetos para explorar, começando fácil e se tornando cada vez mais complexo. Desbloqueie quebra-cabeças e categorias posteriores, preenchendo os anteriores, e finalize projetos no orçamento para ganhar dicas para ajudá-lo mais tarde. O Transplan apoia totalmente as conquistas e salva em nuvem para que o seu progresso esteja com você em qualquer lugar!

reviews.review:
TransPlan is a clever physics puzzle game that takes an extremely simple objective and gradually transforms it into a surprisingly demanding exercise in experimentation. Developed and published by Kittehface Software, the game asks you to move a payload from one location to another using a limited collection of tools and the natural behavior of its physics system. There is no need for an elaborate story or complicated progression structure because the satisfaction comes almost entirely from constructing an idea, watching it succeed or collapse, and adjusting the design until everything works.

The puzzles initially appear straightforward. You have a destination, an object that needs to reach it, and tools such as ramps and catapults that can manipulate its movement. Once the stages become more elaborate, however, understanding momentum, gravity, positioning, trajectories, and collisions becomes increasingly important. A tiny change in the angle of a ramp can determine whether the payload reaches its destination or falls hopelessly short. The game consequently rewards observation as much as logical reasoning, since every unsuccessful attempt provides information that can be used to improve the next one.

One of TransPlan's greatest strengths is that failure rarely feels completely wasted. Watching an object tumble through your carefully assembled setup can be amusing, but it also reveals where the design went wrong. This creates an enjoyable rhythm of planning, testing, observing, and rebuilding. Rather than providing one obvious solution, the physics-based design encourages players to approach situations creatively. Some puzzles can inspire unnecessarily complicated contraptions before the player realizes that a much simpler arrangement accomplishes the same objective.

There are dozens of projects to complete, with earlier challenges introducing the fundamental mechanics before later categories become available. This progression allows the difficulty to grow without immediately overwhelming newcomers. Completing previous projects unlocks additional content, providing a clear sense of advancement even though the game remains firmly focused on individual puzzle scenarios. Later stages expect players to combine lessons learned from previous experiments, making the journey from simple transportation problems to complicated physics challenges feel natural.

The budget mechanic adds another worthwhile dimension. Reaching the destination is important, but completing a project efficiently provides an additional goal. Staying within the assigned budget rewards economical construction and can earn hints that become useful during more challenging projects. This encourages players to revisit solutions that technically work but use more resources than necessary. A messy arrangement might achieve the objective, while an elegant solution accomplishes it with fewer components. For puzzle enthusiasts who enjoy optimization, this substantially increases the incentive to refine completed stages.

Its hand-drawn visual presentation gives TransPlan an identity that suits the concept remarkably well. Each project resembles an engineering sketch or an experiment drawn inside a notebook. The graphics are intentionally modest, but they communicate the necessary information without excessive visual clutter. Instead of attempting realism, the game embraces a scrapbook-like aesthetic that makes its mechanical experiments feel playful. The understated presentation also helps keep attention on the puzzle itself.

The simplicity does come with limitations. Players expecting storytelling, characters, exploration, combat, or a large variety of completely different gameplay systems will not find them here. TransPlan is unapologetically centered on physics puzzles. The trial-and-error structure can also become frustrating when a concept seems correct but requires several small adjustments before it behaves as intended. Precision and patience become increasingly important, so players who dislike repeatedly modifying a solution may find some of the harder projects more irritating than satisfying.

Beyond the main puzzles, the game includes 19 Steam achievements, Steam Cloud functionality, Trading Cards, and Family Sharing support. Cloud saving is particularly convenient for a game based around gradually clearing projects and improving previous results. The interface is available in multiple languages, and the modest hardware requirements reflect the game's lightweight presentation. Windows, macOS, and Linux versions exist, although the older macOS build has compatibility limitations with modern versions of Apple's operating system.

Steam Deck compatibility is currently best regarded as Unverified rather than officially Verified or Playable. The game has a Linux version and relatively modest requirements, which are encouraging characteristics for handheld use, but there is no official Steam Deck compatibility rating displayed for the title. Players specifically purchasing it for Steam Deck should therefore expect that manual adjustments or compatibility considerations may be necessary rather than assuming a completely certified experience.

TransPlan ultimately succeeds through focus. It takes the familiar idea of moving something from point A to point B and builds an entire puzzle experience around discovering increasingly inventive ways to accomplish that task. Its strongest moments come when an apparently impossible arrangement finally works after several experiments, especially when the eventual solution turns out to be simpler than expected. The combination of approachable mechanics, increasingly complicated projects, budget-based optimization, charming hand-drawn presentation, and unpredictable physics makes it an enjoyable choice for players who appreciate thoughtful experimentation. It may be modest in scale, but its puzzles demonstrate how much entertainment can emerge from a small collection of well-integrated mechanics.

Rating: 8/10
